issues.title: review-specs Step 6 captures file-sha before Step 7 status update, causing false drift on next plan invocation
issues.notes: The review SHA (file-sha field in .review.md) is computed and written in Step 6 (Save Review Report). Step 7 then writes the spec file back with status updated from review-pending to review-passed. This changes the file hash, so the very next /adev:plan invocation detects hash drift and blocks planning even though no meaningful content changed. Fix: compute and write file-sha AFTER Step 7 completes the status update, so the stored SHA matches the final on-disk state of the spec.

issues.title: No concurrent-write protection on shared tasks.md — cross-session writes lose data
issues.notes: lib/issues/file-adapter.mjs _write() does a plain readFileSync → mutate-in-memory → writeFileSync sequence with no locking, no atomic rename, and no version check.  Observed failure mode (2026-05-11 during 0.25.0 reconcile session): Three concurrent Claude sessions on the same project directory mutated tasks.md. The background agent (in a separate session) created epic-72 and re-parented issues 274/374 — those changes were visible briefly on disk, then completely wiped by a subsequent write from a different writer that had read an earlier version. Other concurrent changes (epic-65/66/69 closure, epic-70 milestone move, issues 456-458 creation) survived. The pattern is unpredictable last-writer-wins lost-update behavior.  Impact: every multi-session scenario (worktrees, parallel agents, user-plus-agent edits) silently loses work. Issue board state cannot be trusted under concurrent access. This is structurally severe because the issue board is the canonical source of truth for plan/issue/epic state across the lifecycle.  Possible fixes (need spec discussion): 1. File lock via proper-lockfile or fs/promises advisory flock around _read+_write critical section. 2. Atomic write via temp file + rename, plus a version/etag check (compare-and-swap) — read returns a version token; write fails if disk version != staged version, triggering a re-read-and-retry. 3. Move to JSON-with-CAS or SQLite — both give atomicity for free and unblock the json-issue-board-adapter spec (issue-457).  Fits under epic-71 (Agent-Reliable State Artifacts). Probably the highest-priority structural fix in that epic since it underpins all other state-artifact reliability work.; Closed: Validated 2026-05-17 — all 15 AC pass, npm test green, 3 commits on feat/agent-reliable-state-artifacts/concurrent-write-protection branch. issues.title: adev:issues skill prose drops body field silently on json backend create()
issues.notes:
The /adev:issues skill's create-issue prose accepts a body/description argument from the user, but the json backend's IssueManagerInterface.create() silently drops any field except the canonical schema (id, title, status, priority, type, dependencies, notes, next_action, created, updated). The field is named "notes" in the adapter, not "description".

Repro (observed in this session while filing issue-483):
1. Invoke /adev:issues create with a multi-paragraph body argument.
2. Skill calls manager.create({ title, description, type, priority }).
3. The created issue persists with notes="" — the description body is dropped without warning.
4. A follow-up manager.update(id, { notes }) is required to attach the body.

Impact:
- User-supplied issue bodies (repro steps, acceptance criteria, links) are silently lost on first create.
- Agent must do a defensive create-then-update dance to attach any body, or the skill prose must teach the agent to use notes (not description).
- No error is surfaced — the silent drop is the worst failure mode for a write API.

Two valid fixes (orthogonal — both prose-level, no behavioral change to the helper):
A) Update skills/issues/SKILL.md to consistently use "notes" instead of "description"/"body" when describing the create arguments, and add an explicit note that the body field is named "notes".
B) Update the json adapter's create() to accept and normalize a "description" alias to "notes" (still write to the same column).

Recommend option A (prose-only, fewer surfaces to keep in sync).

Affected files (audit needed):
- skills/issues/SKILL.md — "Create Issue" section and argument descriptions
- Any other SKILL.md that invokes /adev:issues create (notably /adev:plan and /adev:implement which auto-create issues)
- lib/issues/json-adapter.mjs (or wherever create() lives) — confirm the dropped-field behavior

Discovered while filing issue-483 in the same /adev:debug session (2026-05-14). See also: issue-483 is the original build-state path-drift bug that exposed this one.

Acceptance criteria:
- skills/issues/SKILL.md create-issue arguments documented using the field name the adapter actually stores

Validate dispatches consume disproportionate tokens — averaged ~90-110K per spec across 13 checks during the lifecycle-artifacts charter build (~3x the per-implement cost). Most checks re-read the same spec, charter, and manifest files independently.

## Problem
Measured during 2026-05-15 lifecycle-artifacts charter retro:
- 11 validate dispatches × ~95K tokens avg = ~1.05M tokens
- 11 implement dispatches × ~25K tokens avg = ~275K tokens
- Validate is ~3x the cost of implement despite doing strictly less work (read-only verification vs. authoring code+tests)

Root cause: every check (1, 1.5, 1.6, 2-13) loads the same spec/charter/manifest files independently inside its own subagent context. No shared cache.

4. Consider whether some checks should be deduped or combined (e.g., Check 1 + 1.5 + 1.6 all read npm test output).

- 30% token reduction conservatively → ~330K tokens saved per 11-spec charter
- Faster validate wall-clock (less LLM throughput on redundant reads)
- Cleaner check authoring contract (signature: (parsedContext) => result)

issues.title: Document worker-vs-orchestrator fork pattern in skill frontmatter
issues.notes:
## Background
The single most important architectural pattern in adev — coordinator/orchestrator skills must NOT fork; worker skills SHOULD fork — is currently undocumented in any skill frontmatter and in using-adev. This caused ~50K tokens + several round-trips of wasted debugging during the 2026-05-15 lifecycle-artifacts charter build before commit f635b6a removed `context: fork` from `skills/build/SKILL.md`.

## The pattern
When invoked via the Skill tool, a skill with `context: fork` in its frontmatter runs in a forked subagent execution context that does NOT inherit the Agent dispatcher tool. This is correct behavior for WORKERS (which are themselves dispatched by an orchestrator via Agent and run in a clean subagent context with its own tool list). It is INCORRECT for ORCHESTRATORS like /adev:build, which need Agent to dispatch their pipeline steps.

## Current state (verified post-fix)
| Skill | Role | context: fork | Correct? |
|---|---|---|---|
| skills/build | orchestrator | removed (f635b6a) | yes |
| skills/implement | worker | present | yes |
| skills/deploy | worker | present | yes |
| skills/research | worker | present | yes |

## Proposed scope
1. Add an explanatory comment to each affected SKILL.md frontmatter declaring its role:
   - build: `# role: orchestrator — must NOT use context: fork (needs Agent dispatcher)`
   - implement/deploy/research: `# role: worker — context: fork is required for context isolation when dispatched by an orchestrator`
2. Add a section to skills/using-adev/SKILL.md documenting the pattern with examples and the failure mode it prevents.
3. Optionally add an integration test that asserts orchestrator skills do NOT carry `context: fork` and worker skills DO carry it.

issues.description:
---

## Investigation findings (2026-05-15)

### (i) Zombie check audit — Checks 3 and 4 at 100% PASS

Sampled 12 random Check 3 PASS bodies + 12 Check 4 PASS bodies from the 78-report corpus.

**Check 3 (Charter Consistency) — verdict: DROP**

Findings:
- Real verification when present: cites specific charter capabilities, entities, and interface contracts.
- BUT transitively redundant given Check 2 (file:line spec compliance with anti-fabrication rule) + review-specs/structural-architect #3 (spec-time scope check).
- 2 of 12 samples were thin/formulaic ("Format Documentation capability (Phase 2, nice-to-have)" was the entire body); 1 was empty.
- The 100% PASS rate is explained by the redundancy chain, not gaming.

Recommendation: replace with a Check 2 sub-finding "scope expansion detected" that fires when code lives outside the spec's listed file scope.

**Check 4 (Constitution Compliance) — verdict: KEEP, tighten contract**

Findings:
- Samples show genuine code-level inspection: import lists, file extensions, version parity in two files, naming conventions.
- These checks cannot be done by review-specs (which works from spec text, not code).
- 100% PASS rate is explained by upstream pipeline enforcing constraints (charter → spec → review → plan → implement); Check 4 is the safety net.

Recommendation: keep, but the new validate charter should codify "every Check 4 finding cites grep / file-inspection evidence" — most samples already do this; make it mandatory.

### (ii) Check 12 noise audit — 49% WARN rate

Pulled all 25 Check 12 WARN sections; classified sub-findings.

Sub-finding frequency within Check 12 WARNs:
- Plan checkboxes: 25/25 (100%)
- Spec status: 16/25 (64%)
- Issue alignment: 14/25 (56%)
- Charter sync: 12/25 (48%)
- Epic completion: 7/25 (28%)

Findings:
- Bodies overwhelmingly contain bookkeeping observations, not validation failures. Example body: "Spec status: implemented → validated. Charter capability row: promoted to validated. Plan checkboxes: 30/30 marked complete." That is a success log labeled WARN.
- Other typical pattern: "Issue alignment: WARN — issues still open but implementation complete." The validator is correctly seeing what `--fix` would update — but `--fix` is opt-in, so the WARN persists every run.
- Plan-checkbox sub-check fires in 100% of WARNs, often on "summary checkboxes" that aren't task state per plan-task-events.spec.md. Retro item #7 confirmed at scale.

Verdict: MOVE to /adev:reconcile, with `--fix` as the default mode. Validation should answer "does code work and match spec"; reconciliation should answer "are bookkeeping artifacts in sync." Bundling them produced 49% noise rate.

## Updated KEEP/MOVE/DROP map (input to /adev:brainstorm)

| Check | Verdict | Destination | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|

issues.title: Auto-recover from stale tasks.json.lock (orphan-lock cleanup)
issues.notes:
The CAS layer in lib/issues/json-adapter.mjs acquires tasks.json.lock via O_EXCL before each write and releases it in the finally block. If the process is killed mid-write (SIGKILL, OS crash, container OOM), the lock file persists. Every subsequent CAS mutator then hits EEXIST → STALE_BOARD_WRITE_RETRY → bounded retry → STALE_BOARD_WRITE. The issue board becomes effectively read-only until someone manually deletes the orphan lock. The error message does not mention the lock file, making the failure hard to debug.

.gitignore now excludes the lock file (committed in ba44d3b on the concurrent-write-protection branch) so it cannot propagate via git, but in-place developer environments still need recovery.

Proposed mitigation: when _write encounters EEXIST on the lock acquire, stat the existing lock file. If its mtime is older than a configurable threshold (default 30 seconds; override via manifest.tasks.cas_lock_stale_seconds), treat it as orphaned, unlink it, and retry the acquire (without consuming a CAS retry budget slot). Log a one-time warning on the recovery path so users notice if it happens repeatedly.

Surfaced 2026-05-17 during PR review of concurrent-write-protection. Filed at user direction as a follow-up; not in scope for the original spec.; Closed: [object Object]

issues.title: specify and implement skills emit step-completed without verdict, blocking downstream gates
issues.notes:
Two skills emit `adev report --type step --status completed` without a verdict, which causes the next skill's gate (`adev gate require`) to block until an operator manually re-emits the completed event with --verdict.

Affected skills:
- skills/specify/SKILL.md:465 — emits `adev report --type step --step specify --status completed` (no verdict). /adev:review-specs then blocks until verdict is re-emitted.
- skills/implement/SKILL.md:37 — emits `adev report --type step --step implement --status completed` (no verdict). /adev:validate then blocks.

Observed twice during 2026-05-17 lifecycle run on tree-sitter-repomap/non-code-reference-detection:
- After /adev:specify, /adev:review-specs blocked with: "step 'review' requires prior step 'specify' to be completed with PASS or PASS_WITH_NOTES (current: {status: completed, verdict: null})". Workaround: manually re-emitted specify completion with --verdict PASS.
- After /adev:implement, /adev:validate blocked with the same shape of error against the 'implement' prior step. Same workaround applied.

Alternative considered (option B — rejected): relax the gate to accept `status: completed` without a verdict for steps that don't naturally produce pass/fail. Rejected because it weakens the gate's contract for the three steps (review, plan, validate) that DO produce verdicts.

Acceptance:

- A clean end-to-end lifecycle (specify → review → plan → implement → validate) succeeds without any manual verdict re-emission.

issues.title: Research: unify quality gates and validation checks under a single logic
issues.notes:
Surfaced 2026-05-17 during /adev:validate scoping discussion on the incremental-artifact-writes spec. The user observed that we have two adjacent concepts with significant overlap and asked whether they should be one thing.

=== Current state (two parallel surfaces) ===

1. **Quality gates** (governance/gates.yaml) — tier-organized commands (fast | integration | e2e), each with kind (deterministic | probabilistic), severity (error | warning), required flag, triggers list (post-task | post-implement | pre-merge), group (smoke | full for e2e). Run by:
   - /adev:validate Check 1 (full tier sweep)
   - /adev:implement post-task hook (via gate triggers)
   - /adev:plan during planning context loading
   - CI directly (npm test, etc.)

2. **Validation checks** (governance/validate.yaml) — registry of checks with kinds (quality-gate | subagent-review | deterministic-check | observational), each with profile, fail-fast, after dependencies, severity. Run by /adev:validate only.

=== Friction points ===

- Check 1 of validation IS the quality-gate tier sweep — wrapper around governance/gates.yaml. Same logic, two entry points.
- Mental model gap: "what must pass before X" has no single answer. Quality gates? Validation checks? Transition gates (governance/gates.yaml transitions section)? All three?
- governance/ has three files (gates.yaml, validate.yaml, boundaries.yaml) that interact in non-obvious ways.
- check-set-restructure.spec.md already relocated 7 historic checks to other skills (review-specs, hygiene, reconcile, post-validate hook). The remaining 5–8 dispatched checks are a hybrid of "gate-like" and "review-like" work.
- Severity, fail-fast, and tier semantics are duplicated across gates.yaml (severity, tier) and validate.yaml (severity, fail_fast, after).

=== Possible unifications to study ===

A. **Single registry** — collapse gates.yaml + validate.yaml + transitions into one governance/checks.yaml with a uniform schema. Each entry declares: id, kind, trigger (when to run), severity, dependencies, command-or-skill-or-subagent.

B. **Layered registries with shared schema** — keep separate files for separation of concerns but make gates a subtype of validation-checks (kind: quality-gate already exists in validate.yaml). Validation checks include their own gates inline.

C. **Trigger-driven dispatcher** — separate from gates/checks files; introduce a "lifecycle event → check set" mapping (post-task fires gates with trigger:post-task; pre-merge fires all gates + all error-severity checks; etc.). Existing gate triggers list is the seed.

D. **Status quo + better docs** — accept the two-surface model and document the boundary clearly. Cheaper but doesn't reduce friction.

=== Research questions ===

- Are there projects with similar two-surface friction? (ESLint/Prettier vs Jest, or Bazel's test/build distinction, or pre-commit/pre-push hook divisions.) What did they pick?
- Does check-set-restructure's relocation logic suggest a deeper unification or argue against it?
- How much complexity is per-check kind (subagent-review needs profile/prompt; deterministic-check needs command; quality-gate needs tier/command/severity)? Could a uniform schema absorb all three without over-engineering?
- Migration cost — gates.yaml is well-established; breaking the surface risks invalidating existing projects' configurations.
- What's the user-facing benefit? One mental model? Faster CI? Fewer governance files? Clearer "what fails what" diagnostics?

=== Out of scope ===

- Implementation work — this is /adev:research first, then potentially spec → plan → implement.
- Lifecycle event log unification — that's already done by agent-reliable-state-artifacts.
- Existing ADRs covering this — none found; this would be a net-new ADR if unification is chosen.

=== Next action ===

Run /adev:research on "unifying quality gates and validation checks under a single logic". Output: research artifact with the four options enumerated above, plus comparable patterns from ESLint/Bazel/pre-commit, plus a recommendation. If recommendation is "unify", file a follow-up spec; if "document the boundary", file a docs task.

issues.title: /adev:route mutates plan files — sibling .routing.md fix + cursor-provider 5-plan migration
issues.notes:
Source: cursor-provider retro 2026-05-19 + /adev:debug subagent transcript (agent ID affc19ea4ef7212c7).
Consolidated re-filing after the prior issue-525 + issue-528 entries were lost in an external rollback of the shared tasks.json.

## The bug

/adev:route Step 4 (skills/route/SKILL.md:108-133) is explicitly instructed to write **Routing:** / **Scores:** / **Rationale:** blocks into each task header inside the plan markdown file. This runs AFTER /adev:plan Step 7 (skills/plan/SKILL.md:678-701) has already emitted plan_task pending events to the lifecycle log.

This directly violates the authoritative-channel invariant CON-8 in agent-reliable-state-artifacts/plan-task-events.spec.md:50-58 ("Plan markdown is read-only after authoring ... /adev:plan writes the plan file once") and AC bullet 5 ("Plan markdown files are not mutated by /adev:plan or /adev:implement after initial authoring").

The detector in lib/plan-immutability.mjs correctly catches this for untracked plans. Cursor-provider plans A-E currently "pass" the detector only because they were committed as a single add (no --diff-filter=M history), which masks rather than fixes the violation.

Reproduction (during cursor-provider session 2026-05-19): both Spec D (cli-install-integration.plan.md) and Spec E (sync-target-output.plan.md) plans had filesystem mtime 2-3 minutes later than their first plan_task pending event in the lifecycle log. Once the plans were committed in d0f8303 and 199928a, the detector relaxed (relied on git history instead of mtime). The underlying violation persists.

## Design decision required

Two viable approaches:
  (a) Sibling .routing.md — /adev:route writes <plan-stem>.routing.md keyed by task ID; /adev:implement reads from it. Preserves human readability, adds one file per plan. Matches the .blockers.md pattern already adopted in commit 7e333fd for review BLOCK handling.
  (c) Lifecycle-log plan_task_routing event — /adev:route emits one event per task into the existing JSONL; /adev:implement reads it like other lifecycle state. No new file, but harder for humans to inspect routing decisions at a glance.

Variant (b) auto-commit-after-plan was rejected during /adev:debug — it silences the immutability detector via git history but still violates CON-8 prose ("read-only after authoring"), and forces an uncommitted-plans-impossible workflow.

Recommendation: variant (a) for consistency with the .blockers.md sidecar pattern.

## Files to change (variant a)

  - skills/route/SKILL.md:108-133 — Step 4: rewrite to write sibling .routing.md instead of mutating plan
  - skills/route/SKILL.md:168-174 — Integration with /adev:implement: point reader at sidecar
  - skills/route/SKILL.md:193 — Red Flag: tighten to "never modify the plan file"
  - skills/implement/SKILL.md — reader change: load routing from sibling .routing.md
  - .context-index/specs/features/agent-reliable-state-artifacts/plan-task-events.spec.md:50-58 — CON-8: enumerate .routing.md as a permitted peer artifact (alongside .review.md, .validate.md, .blockers.md)

## Migration of 5 already-mutated cursor-provider plans

Once the fix lands, the existing plans on the cursor-provider/cursor-adapter branch will have stale inline annotations. Affected:
  - .context-index/specs/features/cursor-provider/hook-config-generator.plan.md (Spec A)
  - .context-index/specs/features/cursor-provider/cursor-adapter.plan.md (Spec B)
  - .context-index/specs/features/cursor-provider/plugin-manifest-and-parity.plan.md (Spec C)
  - .context-index/specs/features/cursor-provider/cli-install-integration.plan.md (Spec D)
  - .context-index/specs/features/cursor-provider/sync-target-output.plan.md (Spec E)

Two migration options:
  (i) Extract: parse each plan, lift the **Routing:**/**Scores:**/**Rationale:** blocks into a new sibling .routing.md, rewrite the plan body without them, stamp the M-commit hash into manifest.yaml hygiene.plan_immutability.exempt_commits[]. Cleanest end state, more work.
  (ii) Leave as historical noise: do not rewrite. New /adev:route invocations on these plans would refuse to write (plan is locked), so any re-routing requires manual extraction. Simpler, but leaves the plans with inline annotations that future readers may mistake for the canonical format.

## Followups flagged in /adev:debug

  1. Draft an ADR titled "Plan-adjacent sidecar artifacts" documenting the .routing.md and .blockers.md sidecar pattern with rationale grounded in the authoritative-channel invariant. The pattern is now used twice (route + review BLOCK in commit 7e333fd) so a single ADR captures both.
  2. Extend lib/plan-immutability.mjs to catch the "mutate-then-single-add-commit" pattern by checking plan body for inline **Routing:** blocks when no sibling .routing.md exists. Would have caught Specs A-E despite their clean git history.
  3. Audit /adev:validate, /adev:review-specs, /adev:debug for any other plan-file writers — same invariant applies.

## History note

The original /adev:debug invocation that produced this diagnosis was filed in this session against issues that were subsequently lost when the shared tasks.json was rolled back externally. The diagnosis is preserved in the /adev:debug subagent transcript (agent ID affc19ea4ef7212c7) and in the retro at .context-index/hygiene/retros/2026-05-19-cursor-provider.md.

Re-filed on 2026-05-19 (consolidated from prior lost issue-525 + issue-528).

issues.title: Surface domain extensions during adev init (extension picker / discovery hint)
issues.notes:
## Problem

A user installing adev into a new project sees only the bundled `software` domain. The framework has already moved non-software domains into installable extension packages (`extensions/data-engineering/`, `extensions/process-automation/`, both with validated specs PASS), and the install pipeline (`adev extension install <source>`) is fully implemented in `cli/index.mjs:956-997` and `lib/extensions/install.mjs`. But `adev init` (or the equivalent install wizard) does not mention extensions at all — there is no discovery surface telling the user that data-engineering, process-automation, or future domains are available.

Symptom: the user picks software-with-wrong-fit, or writes a custom domain from scratch (re-discovering `extends: software` + `.context-index/domains/<name>/` + `domain: <name>` in manifest.yaml), or simply does not realize extensions exist.

## Charter context

`.context-index/specs/features/domain-extensions/charter.md:29` *explicitly* lists "Auto-install during `adev init`" as out of scope for v1 of the extension work. The wording "for v1" was deliberate — that v1 was the content+pipeline; the install-UX bridge is the natural v2 follow-on. This issue is that follow-on.

## Recommended fix

Add an extension-discovery prompt to the init flow. Two implementation paths, ranked:

1. **First-party catalog with picker** *(preferred)*. After the providers prompt and before the context-index scaffold step, scan a known set of first-party extensions (start with the two that exist: `data-engineering`, `process-automation`). Present:
   ```
   Heading: Domain Extensions
   Select a domain extension to install (or skip for software-only):
     1. software (bundled) — general-purpose [default]
     2. data-engineering — pipelines, ETL, dbt, data quality
     3. process-automation — workflow automation, CI/CD orchestration
     4. skip
   ```
   On selection, call `installExtension(<path>, projectRoot, opts)` (the same function the CLI verb wraps). The first-party catalog can live as a small JSON manifest in `templates/` or embedded in `cli/index.mjs`. Multi-select also reasonable.

2. **Discovery hint only** *(minimal)*. After init completes, print a one-line note:
   ```
   Tip: To use a domain other than software, install an extension:
         adev extension install ./extensions/data-engineering
         adev extension install <git-url>
         (or browse: https://agentic-dev.org/extensions)
   ```
   No prompt, no install — just discoverability.

Option 1 fixes the UX gap; option 2 reduces it. Both close the report-symptom that prompted this issue.

## Scope

1. Decide between picker (option 1) vs hint (option 2). Picker recommended.
2. If picker: define the first-party catalog (which extensions ship as known options). Start with the two that exist in this monorepo.
3. Wire the catalog into `cli/index.mjs` init/upgrade flows.
4. Reuse `installExtension()` from `lib/extensions/install.mjs` for the actual install — no new install machinery.
5. Persist the choice in `manifest.yaml` (`domain: <name>` plus extension stamp via existing `readManifestStamps()` flow).
6. Update `skills/init/SKILL.md` to walk the user through the picker.
7. Update the install-completion message to confirm which domain extension (if any) was selected.
8. Test: integration test exercising init with each catalog choice.

## Acceptance criteria

- `adev init` surfaces available domain extensions to the user.
- User can select one (or skip) without leaving the init flow.
- Selected extension is installed via the existing `installExtension()` pipeline.
- `manifest.yaml` is stamped with the chosen domain and extension provenance.
- `adev upgrade` offers the same picker if no domain extension is installed.
- A new project where the user picks data-engineering has working `.context-index/domains/data-engineering/` after init (or whatever path the extension resolves to).
- The install-completion message shows the selected domain.

## References

- Charter (and out-of-scope note): `.context-index/specs/features/domain-extensions/charter.md:29`
- Install verb implementation: `cli/index.mjs:956-997`
- Install pipeline: `lib/extensions/install.mjs`
- Existing first-party extensions: `extensions/data-engineering/`, `extensions/process-automation/`
- Adjacent open issues: issue-447 (extract non-software domains), issue-448 (data-engineering package), issue-450 (remove from bundled templates) — those address packaging; this issue addresses discoverability/install UX, which they do not.
- Source of report: a user installing adev into a new project who only saw `software` and did not realize extensions were available.

issues.title: Author docs/cli-reference.md — agent-facing CLI verb reference for all 24 verbs
issues.notes:
## Problem

`adev help` shows 5 of 24 CLI verbs. The remaining 19 (gate, report, build-state, partial, heuristics, source-manifest, domain, context, verify, state, execution-state, preflight, prototype, artifact, issues, diagnose, etc.) are referenced only in scattered SKILL.md prose. Agents looking for verb signatures or argument shapes have to (a) grep `cli/index.mjs` for the dispatch table, (b) read multiple SKILL.md files, or (c) run `node cli/index.mjs <verb> --help` against guesses. None of these is a usable discovery surface.

Confirmed by a session audit (2026-05-20): the agent-load path (SessionStart hook → using-adev SKILL.md → CLAUDE.md → Context Routing table) contains zero pointers to a CLI verb reference. `docs/skill-reference.md` exists for the /adev:* skills but there is no equivalent for the underlying CLI verbs.

## Recommended fix

Create `docs/cli-reference.md` mirroring the format and tone of `docs/skill-reference.md`. One section per CLI verb, grouped by audience.

## Scope

1. New file `docs/cli-reference.md` with two top-level sections:
   - **User-facing verbs** (5): `install`, `upgrade`, `uninstall`, `extension`, `migrate`. These are the public surface invoked via `npx @adev-org/adev-cli <verb>`.
   - **Lifecycle / internal verbs** (~19): `gate`, `report`, `build-state`, `partial`, `heuristics`, `source-manifest`, `domain`, `context`, `verify`, `state`, `execution-state`, `preflight`, `prototype`, `artifact`, `issues`, `diagnose`, `init`, `status`, `help`. These are invoked from SKILL.md prose and by other CLI verbs; agents need them for orchestration.
2. Per-verb entry format: one-line description, full argument signature (flags + types + defaults), one example invocation, link to implementing module (`lib/cli/<verb>.mjs` or anchor in `cli/index.mjs`), cross-references to relevant SKILL.md files that invoke it.
3. Add `docs/cli-reference.md` to `docs/README.md` under the Reference section (next to `skill-reference.md`).
4. Update the `using-adev` SKILL.md's existing reference to drop the 'when present' qualifier once the file lands.
5. Tests: optionally add a script-based check that every verb in the `cli/index.mjs` dispatch table has a corresponding section in `docs/cli-reference.md` (drift guard). Can ship as a v2 follow-on.

## Acceptance criteria

- `docs/cli-reference.md` exists and documents all 24 verbs currently registered in `cli/index.mjs`.
- Each verb has: one-line description, full argument signature, at least one example, link to implementing file.
- Verbs are grouped into user-facing vs lifecycle/internal sections.
- `docs/README.md` lists the new file under Reference.
- `skills/using-adev/SKILL.md` qualification ('when present') is removed.
- Spot-check: an agent asked about a specific verb (e.g., `adev partial`) should be able to answer from the new doc without reading source.

- CLI dispatch table source: `cli/index.mjs:1424-1450` (verb registry)

issues.title: Config-driven skill model binding via /adev:sync
issues.description:
Long-term replacement for the hardcoded `model:` frontmatter introduced in skills/build/SKILL.md alongside issue-497. Wires Claude Code's skill-frontmatter `model:` field into the existing `model_tiers` mechanism so SKILL.md sources stay provider-agnostic per model-routing.spec.md.

## Background
Claude Code skill frontmatter supports a `model:` field that pins the model for the skill's turn (docs: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md). adev's cross-cutting `model-routing.spec.md` (AC: 'No SKILL.md file contains a hardcoded model name') forbids concrete model IDs in SKILL.md sources — they should declare a tier (`fast` / `capable` / `reasoning`) and resolve at runtime from `platform-context.yaml:model_tiers`.

These two facts conflict: the frontmatter parser is static YAML, so a tier name there is meaningless to Claude Code. The reconciliation is a build-time materialization: bind skills to tiers in `manifest.yaml`, and have `/adev:sync` resolve the binding and write the concrete model ID into the on-disk SKILL.md frontmatter.

Issue-497 lands a one-off hardcoded `model: claude-sonnet-4-6` in `skills/build/SKILL.md` to ship the Sonnet migration on milestone 0.28.0. This issue tracks replacing that hardcode with the config-driven mechanism.

## Scope
1. Manifest schema: add `skill_models:` block. Keys are skill names (e.g. `adev:build`); values are tier names (`fast` / `capable` / `reasoning`).
2. CLI verb `adev model apply`: reads `skill_models`, resolves each tier from `platform-context.yaml:model_tiers`, writes the resolved model ID into the corresponding SKILL.md frontmatter `model:` line. Idempotent.
3. `--check` mode: exit non-zero if any bound skill's on-disk `model:` value disagrees with the resolved binding. For CI / pre-commit.
4. `/adev:sync` integration: invoke `adev model apply` as part of the sync flow so updating the binding propagates automatically.
5. Amend `model-routing.spec.md` to document the rendered-vs-source distinction (source SKILL.md MAY contain `model:` populated by the apply step; manual edits to that field are discouraged).
6. Replace the hardcoded `model: claude-sonnet-4-6` in `skills/build/SKILL.md` with the binding flow: declare `"adev:build": capable` in manifest, run apply.

## Acceptance
- `skill_models` schema is documented in manifest.yaml + templates/manifest.yaml.tmpl
- `adev model apply` resolves tiers and writes frontmatter; tests cover write, idempotency, missing-tier fallback, malformed-binding rejection.
- `adev model apply --check` returns non-zero on drift; CI / pre-commit can use it.
- `/adev:sync` runs the apply step automatically.
- `model-routing.spec.md` amended to reflect the source-vs-rendered model contract.
- `skills/build/SKILL.md` switched from hardcode to binding; existing Sonnet behavior preserved.

## References
- issue-497 — short-term hardcoded migration (this is the long-term replacement)
- issue-501 — cost ticker (independent, but enables A/B measurement of the binding's effect)
- `.context-index/specs/cross-cutting/model-routing.spec.md` — invariant being preserved
- `skills/build/SKILL.md:54` — currently makes an aspirational claim about `model_routing.subagent_overrides` that this work makes real (under a different schema name)

issues.title: adev gates doctor: verify declared gates actually run and tests actually get collected
issues.notes: HIGHEST-LEVERAGE finding of the 2026-08-10 three-repo audit (adev-plugin, repo-B, repo-C accelerator). All three repos wrote tests that never executed, and adev never noticed: adev-plugin’s npm test glob silently skipped 67 files / ~1,000 cases (sh has no globstar, so tests/**/*.test.mjs == tests/*/*.test.mjs); repo-B CI ran only 19% of test files and ZERO Python tests (70k LOC, ~3,000 test fns, never run in CI); repo-C had no CI at all, pytest was not even a dependency, and its declared gates cd into a gitignored repo so they cannot execute. issues.title: End-to-end test-depth enforcement: verify authored suites match their assigned depth
issues.notes: Descoped from test-depth-policy at revision 6 (see its Scope Boundary section). That spec assigns and records a depth per task; nothing verifies the authored suite matches it. Round-5 review established why enforcement could not be bolted on, all verified against code: (1) write-handoff.mjs:43-46 hashes test file CONTENTS only, so any depth field added to Handoff Block frontmatter is unattested and written by the same subagent being checked — structurally identical to the existing self-reported gaming_check: passed. (2) "Case classes actually covered" has no machine-decidable definition; lib/test-strategies/gaming.mjs is depth-invariant by design so nothing computes it. (3) Packets are keyed on a spec-derived slug and overwritten each RED run (immutable-handoff-block.spec.md:37,41), so under the shipped per-behavior default N tasks share one packet and a later task destroys an earlier record. (4) A git-diff check cannot run at suite acceptance: that point is RED-complete so the source edits happen later in GREEN, and git diff --name-only cannot see the untracked files a Create: task produces. Doing this properly requires: amending immutable-handoff-block.spec.md (per spec-amendment-artifacts.spec.md) for packet keying and content; giving conformance evidence a per-task key; relocating the check to task-commit time against a pinned base plus git ls-files -o; and deciding whether raising a shared suite is permitted given the hash lock. Also unresolved and belonging here: nothing enforces that assert-assigned is called at all (under /adev:implement --parallel, group subagents run the TDD loop from prose inside worktrees), and depth is not reconciled across tasks sharing a suite. || DESIGN DECISION (human, 2026-08-13): shared suites ARE permitted; packets get re-keyed per task. Amend immutable-handoff-block.spec.md so packet keys are task-scoped (not spec-slug-scoped) and conformance evidence is per-task, replacing the current one-packet-per-spec-slug scheme. This (a) unblocks issue-614's 'prefer extending an existing suite' guidance, which the content-hash lock otherwise makes unworkable, and (b) fixes the existing bug where N tasks sharing a spec slug overwrite one another's packet (immutable-handoff-block.spec.md:37,41). Rejected alternatives: keeping one-suite-per-task and making plan tasks coarser (leaves the packet-overwrite bug, fights natural per-module test grouping); and specing 559 as detection-only (sidesteps the hash question but leaves depth unenforced, contradicting the audit's core lesson that prose does not bind — only deterministic gates do). issue-559 and issue-614 should be designed and implemented as ONE effort.

issues.title: Author one regression rubric per skill epic-102 intends to change, BEFORE changing it
issues.notes:
MEASURED 2026-08-13. 32 rubric files exist across 7 eval directories, which overstates coverage badly. Only THREE are per-skill compression-regression rubrics — tests/evals/skill-compression/rubrics/{brainstorm,plan,specify}.yaml — covering 3 of 30 skills, and one of those three (plan) sits on the broken variant matrix in issue-620. The other 29 rubrics score different things: whole-workflow scenarios (work-tracking, configurable-governance), domain-level project comparisons (comparison/), infrastructure honesty (integration-sandbox), and a data-domain set (data-engineering). A rubric that scores a six-step lifecycle scenario tells you the pipeline ran; it cannot tell you that /adev:route's scoring degraded after its prose was compressed.

THIRTEEN skills have no rubric mention at all: codehealth, deploy, init, learn, prototype, reconcile, recover, repomap, research, retro, sample, sync, using-adev.

THE OVERLAP THAT MAKES THIS URGENT: the skills epic-102 queues for demotion, merging and deletion are almost exactly the skills with no coverage. issue-573 targets codehealth, repomap, document, deploy, sync; issue-574 targets learn and issues; issue-575 merges eval into validate --score, assess into init --brownfield, and reduces using-adev; issue-576 deletes skills/standalone; issue-571 rewrites prototype. Of those, codehealth / repomap / deploy / sync / learn / using-adev / prototype / standalone have NO rubric, and issues / eval / assess / document are touched only by scenario rubrics. That is not a coincidence — they are the peripheral skills, which is both why they look expendable and why nobody built evals for them. The consequence is that the simplification sweep would run exactly where the regression net is thinnest.

SCOPE: not 30 rubrics. One rubric per skill epic-102 intends to touch — roughly 10 — each authored BEFORE that skill is modified, so the comparison is against a captured baseline rather than a memory of how it used to behave. Cheap to write: the existing scenarios (tests/evals/skill-compression/scenarios/*.md) are self-contained prompts carrying simulated user responses, so runs are reproducible without a human in the loop. Follow the existing rubric shape — regex-matched required_elements (deterministic, 50%) plus weighted quality_dimensions (50%) — with the judged half restructured into BINARY per-criterion verdicts rather than 1-5 scales, per the external research on judge reliability.

SEQUENCING: this is the real gate on epic-102, not a nice-to-have. A rubric authored after a skill is compressed measures the compressed skill against itself. Priority order should follow epic-102's own: 573 and 575 first (they touch the most skills), then 574, 571, 576.

NUANCE for issue-576 (delete skills/standalone): a deleted skill needs a different test, not a compression rubric — assert that the CLI path it wrapped still works and that no caller is stranded. Worth stating explicitly so nobody writes a rubric for a file that is about to vanish.

Reference target from the research digest: 20-50 tasks drawn from real failures, each with a reference solution, outcome-graded, held near 100% as a regression gate. Three compression rubrics is roughly a tenth of that floor.

issues.title: adev pr body: roll commit trailers up into a spec-scoped provenance table
issues.notes:
Every commit carries Spec:, Plan-task:, Issue:, Author-type:, Operator: trailers (manifest.yaml:168-178) and CI validates them per-commit — but nothing rolls them up, so a reviewer opening a 50-file PR gets no map of which hunks trace to which spec.

Foundation for the routing-map and validate-verdict issues. Research: .context-index/research/pr-review-experience.md rec 2.

--- Forge-neutrality constraint (2026-08-12) ---
MUST emit markdown to stdout and know nothing about any forge. Its inputs (commit trailers, <spec>.routing.json, the validate report) are adev artifacts that exist in every adev project by construction, so the content layer is 100% provider-agnostic — it works on GitLab, Gitea, Bitbucket, Forgejo, a bare remote, or email-a-patch with zero changes. Whoever pipes stdout into a forge is a separate, project-specific concern.

Do NOT build a forge adapter as part of this issue. When adev is first run against a non-GitHub forge, add a registry following lib/issues/registry.mjs (json/file/beads -> adapter, graceful fallback when the binary is missing), which itself follows lib/provider/registry.mjs. NAMING TRAP: do not call the knob `provider` — that word already means agent harness (claude-code / opencode / codex / cursor / copilot) in lib/provider/registry.mjs. Use `forge:` or `completion.forge:`.

Note also that lib/milestones.mjs's `execGh` is NOT a portability seam despite appearances: it is named for gh and passes gh-shaped argv (["pr","list","--head",...]), so it is a test injection point only. A real adapter needs semantic verbs (postReviewComment(id, body)), not argv passthrough.

--- Depends on issue-588 (wired 2026-08-12) ---

The session-capture installer currently corrupts it (sentinel wrapper leaves a dangling `if`, bash syntax error at line 43), so commits made through a corrupted hook may carry no trailers at all. Fix the emitter before building the aggregator on top of it.

--- Constraint from issue-582 (NOT a blocking dep) ---
issue-582 (Spec: trailer -> node -e command injection) is marked in_progress on the board but the fix ALREADY LANDED on main via PR #214: .githooks/post-commit:61 now exports ADEV_PC_SPECS_TOUCHED and lib/session-summary.mjs reads env.ADEV_PC_SPECS_TOUCHED — no JS interpolation. CONSTRAINT THAT SURVIVES: issue-582 also observed that the trailer value is emitted into YAML frontmatter UNQUOTED, so a Spec: value containing ] , or a newline corrupts downstream frontmatter parsing. issue-597 consumes the same trailers — it MUST reuse the sanitized path and quote on output, never re-parse raw git trailer text.

issues.title: [GitHub-specific] Make the CI advisory comment sticky instead of delete-and-repost
issues.notes:

issues.title: DECISION: infra-gated suites (Postgres/docker) fail hard, making npm test red without docker — pick a policy
issues.notes:
Surfaced by issue-560 (test discovery fix). Before: sh collapsed the ** glob so 339 of 416 files ran. After: 410 run (6 nested-project fixture suites excluded by rule). Measured 2026-08-12: full suite 5448 tests / 33 fail; the 71 newly-included files run alone give 1112 tests / 31 fail; the original 339-file set alone gives 1 fail (a concurrency flake). So ~31 failures are in code that has never executed in CI. Affected suites: tests/evals/integration-sandbox/* (Phase 1 fixture setup, Phase 3 live-Postgres execution, reality-check fixture + end-to-end Check 12), which expect PostgreSQL on port 5433 with seeded data. They fail hard rather than skip — consistent with the project preference that integration tests must never silently self-skip. Consequence: the single quality gate (npm test) is red on any machine without docker-compose running. Options: (a) keep them in the default run and require docker for a green suite; (b) split into npm run test:integration with an explicit, documented tag and keep npm test unit-only; (c) keep them in-run but let the harness fail with a clear "infra required" message. This is a policy call, not a code fix — do not resolve it by silently excluding the suites.

CORRECTED 2026-08-12 after review. My original framing was wrong: adev-plugin has NO Postgres dependency (root package.json has only tree-sitter deps). The Postgres/docker belongs to tests/evals/integration-sandbox/, a self-contained FIXTURE PROJECT with its own package.json, its own pg dependency, and its own docker-compose.yml, described as a "minimal Node.js + PostgreSQL fixture for testing whether adev skills write honest integration tests against real external infrastructure". Its driver even documents "run `npm run db:up` first" — it is a manually-run eval, never intended for automated npm test. Resolution: tests/evals/** is now a separate opt-in bucket (npm run test:evals), so the default gate no longer depends on machine state. DECISION TAKEN: evals are excluded from the default npm test and run via npm run test:evals. This is NOT the silent-skip pattern to avoid — the split is printed on every run, asserted by tests/test-discovery.test.mjs (buckets must partition every file on disk with no overlap), and reachable by an explicit script. Reversible via npm run test:all.; Closed: Resolved by the eval/default bucket split in scripts/run-tests.mjs; decision recorded on the issue.

issues.title: Issue-board ID allocation is not safe across git branches — two sessions minted the same issue-589
issues.notes:
Reproduced 2026-08-13. lib/issues/json-adapter.mjs derives new IDs via _nextIssueId(issues) — max(existing)+1 against the CURRENT FILE. _withCas protects concurrent writers of one file, and resolveStorageRoot() makes the board shared across worktrees, but nothing protects allocation across git BRANCHES: a session on chore/board-sync-epic-106 minted issue-589 (infra-gated suites decision, epic-105) while a session on main minted issue-589 (regression rubrics, epic-108) from the same 588 baseline. Both were valid locally; the collision only surfaced at merge time. Same hazard for epics (branch took 105-107 while main later referenced an epic-108 that exists on no board).

RESOLVED THIS INSTANCE by renumbering the branch-side entry to issue-612 during the merge (see the board-merge PR), but the mechanism will re-collide the next time board writes live on an unmerged branch.

OPTIONS: (a) make IDs merge-safe (monotonic clock/random suffix, or a per-session prefix) — breaks the human-friendly issue-N convention; (b) keep sequential IDs but add an `adev issues renumber --against <ref>` verb that detects and re-mints collisions at merge time, plus a CI check that fails a PR whose board adds IDs already present on the base branch; (c) policy: board writes only ever land on main via short-lived PRs, never accumulate on long-lived branches (the practice that failed here — this branch carried 26 entries).

Recommend (b)+(c): tooling to make the collision detectable and a policy to keep the window small. (a) is the only true fix but costs the readable IDs the whole framework quotes in prose, commits, and specs.

issues.title: Soften the plan test-file mandate and task granularity that drive test-file explosion
issues.notes: From the 2026-08-10 three-repo audit. The POLICY half of the file-explosion finding; issue-555 covers only detecting the symptom via a hygiene audit pass, not changing the rule that produces it. /adev:plan requires every task to reference or create a test file, combined with 2-5 minute task granularity and the anti-tamper ratchet (handoff hashes make an authored suite effectively append-only). Net effect observed across all three audited repos: one test file per plan task rather than per behavior, with no consolidation pressure — repo-B ships 11 test files for one module and a test_validate_rev6_fulltable_e2e.py-style rev-N chain (43 files reference a 'rev N'); 60% of its Python test files embed a literal 'Task N' (513 occurrences); adev-plugin has describes named '(plan-task 2)'..'(plan-task 9)'. Proposed fix: change the plan rule from 'every task must reference/create a test file' to 'prefer extending an existing suite; create a new file only when no suite covers this behavior', and make the RED phase explicitly permit raising an existing suite. Note the interaction with the handoff-hash lock (see issue-559's notes): allowing a task to extend a shared suite is exactly the case the current hash contract does not cleanly express, so these two should be designed together. || DESIGN DECISION (human, 2026-08-13): shared suites ARE permitted; packets get re-keyed per task. Amend immutable-handoff-block.spec.md so packet keys are task-scoped (not spec-slug-scoped) and conformance evidence is per-task, replacing the current one-packet-per-spec-slug scheme. This (a) unblocks issue-614's 'prefer extending an existing suite' guidance, which the content-hash lock otherwise makes unworkable, and (b) fixes the existing bug where N tasks sharing a spec slug overwrite one another's packet (immutable-handoff-block.spec.md:37,41). Rejected alternatives: keeping one-suite-per-task and making plan tasks coarser (leaves the packet-overwrite bug, fights natural per-module test grouping); and specing 559 as detection-only (sidesteps the hash question but leaves depth unenforced, contradicting the audit's core lesson that prose does not bind — only deterministic gates do). issue-559 and issue-614 should be designed and implemented as ONE effort.
issues.next_action: Design 559+614 together as one effort, starting from the recorded shared-suite/per-task-packet decision. First step: amend immutable-handoff-block.spec.md per spec-amendment-artifacts.spec.md.

issues.title: Cross-layer duplicate test coverage: same invariant asserted at lib, CLI, hook, and e2e layers
issues.notes: From the 2026-08-10 three-repo audit. The one finding with no issue of any kind until now. Roughly 12-15% of test cases in both code repos (adev-plugin, repo-B) assert the same invariant at multiple layers — a rule implemented once in lib/ gets a lib unit test, a CLI-verb test, a hook test, and an e2e test, each re-asserting the identical behavior rather than testing that layer's own contract (wiring, argument parsing, exit codes). Consequence is runtime and maintenance cost with no added defect-detection: a change to the invariant breaks 4 tests that all encode the same fact, while a genuine wiring regression between layers may still slip through untested. Needs measurement before prescription: quantify the true duplication rate (the audit's 12-15% was a sampled estimate, not an exhaustive count), then decide whether the fix is guidance in write-test (assert behavior once at its owning layer; at other layers assert only the delegation) or a detector. Likely overlaps issue-555's hygiene test-debt pass — consider folding in as one more detection there rather than building separate machinery.

issues.title: Falsifiable spec assumptions: pin empirical claims to runnable commands
issues.notes: Option 4 of .context-index/research/review-specs-value-and-shift-left.md. The highest-value review findings are empirical claims about existing code ("write-handoff.mjs:43-46 hashes contents only", "git diff --name-only omits untracked files", "N of 150 plans lack a **Files:** block") — facts a command answers in seconds. They are currently argued in prose across rounds, and one was MEASURED WRONG: round 5 cited "17 of 150 plans", the correct per-task figure is 131 of 149, and discovering that consumed an entire extra round which then reversed a fail-closed parsing decision. FIX: specs gain an assumptions: block of { claim, command, expected }; add "adev spec verify-assumptions" that runs them and records results to the lifecycle log; instruct reviewers that an empirical counter-claim about existing code must be filed as an assumption with a command, not as a prose blocker; /adev:validate re-runs the block post-implementation so a claim that rots is caught. This is the direct fix for review-injected regression — it removes the class of round that exists only to correct a previous round's confident error.

issues.title: Report spec size delta per review round as a review-health signal
issues.notes: Option 6 of .context-index/research/review-specs-value-and-shift-left.md. Review pressure adds prose, and prose is what gets reviewed — a self-feeding loop. test-depth-policy grew 34 KB -> 57 KB (+65%) across an arc whose net effect was REMOVING three behaviors (raise-on-extend, the conformance leg, the evasion leg). Each round's fixes add clarifying clauses, scope-boundary sections and error-code rows, all of which become new surface for the next round to find findings in. Undetected across five rounds. FIX: /adev:review-specs reports spec byte-delta since last-reviewed-revision (both values already tracked); warn when a round whose stated intent was descope grew the spec. Optional soft cap suggesting a split above ~25 KB. Trivial cost — bytes diff against data already on hand.

issues.title: Resolve rigor tier by opening review verdict, not risk level alone
issues.notes: Option 7 of .context-index/research/review-specs-value-and-shift-left.md. Supersedes the naive "default everything to quick tier" reading of the tier A/B. The A/B measured full $16.42 vs quick $5.12 (-69%) at quality 90 vs 88 with verdict parity — but BOTH sampled specs returned PASS_WITH_NOTES in both tiers, so it NEVER exercised a spec that should BLOCK. BLOCK is 7.5% of real rounds on main and the one verdict that predicts further revision with 100% reliability (vs 15.5% for PASS_WITH_NOTES, 26.5% for PASS). FIX: first review runs full (opening verdict is the strongest signal in the dataset and is cheap relative to being wrong); rounds 2+ on a spec sitting at PASS_WITH_NOTES run quick; specs that opened BLOCK stay full throughout. Implementation is a resolution-precedence rule in lib/governance/rigor-mode.mjs — tier machinery already shipped. Keep the security reviewer unconditional in every tier: it is 33% of all real blockers and the most bimodal reviewer in the corpus.

issues.title: Require a disposition on every review warning (fixed / accepted / deferred)
issues.notes: Option 8 of .context-index/research/review-specs-value-and-shift-left.md. PASS_WITH_NOTES is the modal outcome at 70.1% of material rounds on main, statistically unchanged from the 78% measured in the 2026-05 review-validation-restructuring research — that research recommended tracking warning action rate and it was never shipped. With no disposition field the rate cannot be read as either healthy advisory output or ignored noise. issues.title: Retire the 83 prose-matching test files once tier-2 diagnostics replace them
issues.notes: The missing BACKFILL half of issue-557. 557 builds the replacement (tier-2 diagnostic producers for SKILL.md/spec/docs structure) and forbids string-matching prose as a future test deliverable — but it does not touch the existing corpus. Nothing on the board currently migrates or retires it, so without this issue adev would ship the new mechanism while keeping ~10k lines of the old pattern in the suite indefinitely. Found 2026-08-13 when the gap was queried directly; the orchestrator had previously and incorrectly assumed 557 covered remediation. Scale (2026-08-10 audit): ~27% of this repo's test CASES are change-detectors; 103 files import NO production code and only readFileSync a .md and call .includes(). tests/skills/ is ~87% this pattern and tests/docs/ is 100% — together 83 files / ~10k lines / 824 cases with essentially zero production coverage. 340 assertions use the near-tautological includes(x) || includes(y) form. Precedent for the split: epic-104 separates producer fixes (issue-585 spec templates, issue-586 review/validate writer) from the backfill of ~400 existing artifacts (issue-587). epic-108 had the producer half (557) and was missing this one. HARD DEPENDENCY on issue-557: do not delete a prose test until the tier-2 producer that covers its invariant actually ships, or coverage is silently lost rather than migrated. Per-file the decision is three-way, not a blanket delete: (a) invariant now covered by a tier-2 diagnostic -> delete the test; (b) invariant real but NOT expressible as a diagnostic -> rewrite as a behavioral test that imports production code; (c) assertion was tautological (the includes(x) || includes(y) family) -> delete outright, it never tested anything. Requires a per-file audit; the count of files deleted vs rewritten vs dropped should be reported, since 'deleted 83 files' and 'migrated 83 invariants' are very different outcomes. Interacts with issue-555 (its hygiene test-debt pass detects prose-assertion density, so it can measure progress here) and issue-615 (cross-layer duplicate coverage — some prose tests may be duplicates rather than needing migration at all). || SCOPE ESTIMATE CONTESTED 2026-08-13 — RE-MEASURE BEFORE PLANNING. issue-555's shipped test-debt scanner (Audit Pass 23) dogfooded this repo and found PROSE_ASSERTION = 25 files, not the 83-103 this issue was filed with. The numbers measure different things and both are internally valid: 227 test files reference a .md path and 115 reference SKILL.md, but only 25 also clear the 0.5 containment-assertion ratio. The audit counted files that TOUCH markdown (specifically: import no production code and only readFileSync a .md and call .includes()); the scanner counts files whose ASSERTIONS are predominantly markdown containment. A file asserting via assert.match regex rather than .includes() lands in the audit's set but may miss the scanner's ratio. Neither is wrong; they answer different questions. Consequence for this issue: do NOT plan against either figure. Run 'adev test-debt scan' for the low-false-positive set (25), then separately enumerate the audit's criterion (no production import + markdown-only assertions) for the outer bound, and reconcile per-file — the three-way audit below is what actually decides each file, and it will resolve files the ratio heuristic misses. Also note issue-555's validate report says 'Remediation of those files is issue-557 territory' — that is the same error this issue was filed to correct; 557 builds the replacement, THIS issue retires the corpus.
issues.next_action: Blocked on issue-557 shipping tier-2 producers. Then run a per-file three-way audit (covered-by-diagnostic / rewrite-as-behavioral / tautological-delete) and report the split.

issues.title: A review verdict that cannot reach its requester is indistinguishable from a review that never ran
issues.notes: Observed live 2026-08-13 during epic-108 wave 2, twice, in the same session. Class: a review outcome is lost and NEITHER side sees an error. (1) Stranded verdict. A dispatched synthesized reviewer completed a re-review of hygiene-test-debt.spec.md rev 2 and returned PASS_WITH_NOTES, having verified all three round-1 blockers RESOLVED empirically against the real suite. It could not deliver that verdict to the session that requested it (SendMessage: 'no agent named general-purpose is reachable') so it returned the report one level up to the orchestrator. The requesting session, receiving nothing, reasonably concluded the review had been cancelled, wrote 'a re-review was deliberately NOT run' into the .review.md Disposition, and proceeded to implementation. The work was better-verified than its own record claimed. Recovered by hand in commit 18ee9e4b only because the orchestrator happened to be holding the report. At least three other nested agents in the same session hit the identical addressing failure (a plan review that returned Approved, a Task-1 implementation report, a spec-compliance PASS). (2) Same class, different mechanism, already fixed in ed84a277: /adev:review-specs SKILL.md emits 'adev report --type step --verdict BLOCK', which the verb rejects (PASS|PASS_WITH_NOTES|FAIL only), so the review step emitted 'started' with no terminal event. Silent because the validate gate checks 'implement', not 'review' — any later /adev:plan or /adev:review-specs on that spec would have blocked PERMANENTLY. That specific contract mismatch is issue-584; this issue is the general failure mode. Why P1: adev's entire gate model assumes a recorded verdict is a faithful record of whether review happened. Both failures break that assumption silently and in the UNSAFE direction — one loses a PASS (work looks less verified than it is, wasting effort), the other loses a BLOCK terminal (spec wedged forever). Directions worth considering: make a dispatched-review request carry a correlation id the requester polls for rather than relying on push delivery; have the report verb reject unknown verdicts LOUDLY at the call site rather than failing silently; and add a diagnostic for a lifecycle step that emitted 'started' with no terminal event within a run, which is the on-disk signature of both failures.
issues.next_action: Decide the mechanism: correlation-id polling for dispatched reviews, loud rejection of unknown verdicts, and/or a tier-2 diagnostic for started-without-terminal lifecycle steps.

issues.title: gate doctor verifies a different gate set than the one that actually executes
issues.notes: Found 2026-08-13 while running /adev:validate on issue-554. adev gate doctor (issue-552) reads .context-index/governance/gates.yaml DIRECTLY with no domain merge, while every actual consumer (/adev:validate Check 1, /adev:implement Step 2-post) resolves gates through 'adev domain load-gates' -> mergeGates(), which merges the domain starter and drops entries failing validateGate. The two sources disagree in BOTH directions, so the doctor can report a clean bill of health on a gate set that never runs. VERIFIED ON THIS REPO, zero overlap between verified and executed: (a) 'adev gate doctor' reports on exactly one gate -- id 'test', command "npm test" -- and exits 0 with '0 error(s), 1 warning(s)'. (b) 'adev domain load-gates --module unified-gates' on the same repo returns a merged list of TWO ENTIRELY DIFFERENT gates -- 'quality-gate' [npm,test] fast and 'integration-test' [npm,run,--if-present,test:integration] integration, both from the software domain default -- plus the warning INVALID_GATE: Gate 'test' command must be an argv list (array), not a string -- skipped. So the doctor validates a gate the executor discards, and is blind to both gates the executor runs. FAILURE MODE, both directions unsafe: (1) FALSE CLEAN -- a string-form gate is analysed and passed by the doctor while merge-gates.mjs:34-37 silently skips it, so a project whose only gate is string-form runs NOTHING while the doctor says it is fine; here the consequence is masked only because the software domain default happens to also run npm test. (2) BLIND SPOT -- domain-starter and extension-overlay gates are never examined by the doctor at all, which after issue-554 ships is where the default integration tier LIVES; the doctor would never diagnose the very defaults that PR shipped. WHY P1: this is precisely the failure class issue-552 was built to eliminate (the audit's highest-leverage finding was 'tests/gates declared but never executed, and adev never noticed'). A verifier reading a different source than the executor reproduces that bug inside the tool meant to detect it. SCOPE NOTE: the string-form half is pre-existing (merge-gates.mjs already rejects strings on main) and issue-554/PR #253 fixes templates/gates-template.yaml going forward -- header and every commented example now teach argv form. What remains unaddressed: every ALREADY-SCAFFOLDED project still carries a string-form gates.yaml plus a header comment teaching the rejected form (this repo included -- .context-index/governance/gates.yaml:10 still reads 'command: Shell command to execute'), and there is no migration or detection path. FIX DIRECTIONS: have runGateDoctor resolve gates through the same mergeGates path its consumers use (the obvious fix -- doctor and executor must agree by construction); have it explicitly report gates dropped by validateGate as an ERROR-severity finding rather than leaving the loader warning to whoever happens to print it; and add a migration that rewrites string-form commands to argv in existing governance/gates.yaml files, or at minimum a diagnostic that flags them.
