issues.title: BeadsAdapter passes the .beads DIRECTORY as --db; br 0.2.22 requires the .db FILE, so every beads operation fails
issues.notes: Found 2026-08-13 attempting 'adev issues migrate --to beads --include-closed' on this repo (307 issues / 106 epics). The migration failed on the FIRST item and created nothing. REPRODUCTION: (1) br init -> creates a .beads/ DIRECTORY containing beads.db, beads.db-shm, and a .gitignore. (2) lib/issues/beads-adapter.mjs:29 sets this.dbPath = join(projectRoot, '.beads') -- the directory -- and line 54 passes it as ['--db', this.dbPath, ...args]. (3) Every br invocation then fails with: CONFIG_ERROR 'Refusing unsafe configured database leaf <database-authority sha256=...>: expected a regular file, not a symlink or special file'. VERIFIED the path is the whole cause, not the payload: 'br --db <root>/.beads create "plain test title" --type bug' fails identically to a title containing backticks and colons, while 'br --db <root>/.beads/beads.db create "migration probe title" --type bug --json' SUCCEEDS and returns a well-formed issue (id adev-plugin-ou0). MISLEADING SURFACE SYMPTOM worth noting for whoever picks this up: the migrate verb reports MIGRATE_PARTIAL_FAILURE naming the first issue it tried (here issue-582, whose title contains backticks and the word SECURITY), which reads exactly like a shell-quoting or injection bug in the title. It is not -- the adapter uses execFileSync with array args and never invokes a shell. Any title fails. Do not chase the quoting theory. LIKELY CAUSE: generational drift between bd (beads, Go) and br (beads_rust). A bd-to-br-migration skill exists in this environment for exactly this class of change, so the older bd probably accepted a directory for --db while br 0.2.22 requires a regular file. FIX: beads-adapter.mjs:29 should resolve the database FILE, e.g. join(projectRoot, '.beads', 'beads.db'), ideally probing for the actual db filename rather than hardcoding it, and should fail with a clear diagnostic when .beads exists but no db file is found. The path is currently hardcoded with no manifest override (tasks.db_path governs the storage ROOT via resolveStorageRoot, and does not reach this field). IMPACT: the beads backend is completely non-functional against br 0.2.22 -- not merely migration, but every create/update/close/list through BeadsAdapter. NO DATA WAS LOST in the failed attempt: 0 issues created, json board untouched at 307/106, manifest still tasks.backend: json, and the .beads dir was removed. A pre-migration board snapshot is committed at c3d4a875 on branch chore/board-migrate-to-beads.; Closed: ALREADY FIXED ON MAIN by commit 9dc95701 ("make the beads backend work against br 0.2.x"), which landed while this was being worked. Main resolves the *.db file inside .beads/ (preferring beads.db) and omits --db entirely when the workspace is uninitialized so br applies its own auto-discovery. Main also fixes two defects this issue never found: it canonicalizes the path via realpath because br refuses a symlinked parent and macOS /var -> /private/var breaks every call, and _runBr now surfaces stdout when stderr is empty (br reports structured failures as JSON on STDOUT, which is why the original error read as a bare "Command failed"). A local fix was written independently (branch fix/beads-adapter-db-path, commit 14f71cf8, 5 TDD tests) and is DISCARDED as redundant and strictly inferior; it survives in reflog only. Verified fixed: migration against main creates 310 issues + 106 epics with 0 errors.
issues.next_action: Fix beads-adapter.mjs:29 to point at the db file (probe for it rather than hardcoding), add a clear diagnostic when the db file is absent, and add a regression test that would fail against a directory path. Then re-run: br init && adev issues migrate --to beads --include-closed.

issues.title: BeadsAdapter.createEpic delegates to the read-only FileAdapter, so epics can never exist on the beads backend
issues.notes: Found 2026-08-13 immediately after fixing issue-626 (the --db path bug) and retrying 'adev issues migrate --to beads --include-closed' on this repo. SECOND, INDEPENDENT blocker -- structural, not a config or path problem. beads-adapter.mjs:241 has createEpic() delegate unconditionally to this._fileAdapter.createEpic(), and file-adapter.mjs:133-135 is 'async createEpic(_epicData) { throw deprecatedWrite(); }' -- an unconditional throw, because the file (markdown) backend is read-only by design. So epic creation on the beads backend is impossible by construction. The adapter's own header comment states the intent: 'Epic operations are delegated to a FileAdapter instance since beads_rust has no epic concept (hybrid approach per SA-5)' -- but the adapter chosen to hold them cannot be written to, so the hybrid has no writable home for epics. OBSERVED RESULT of the retry: all 308 issues migrated successfully and .beads-map.json holds 308 entries (verified directly: 'br --db .beads/beads.db list --json' returns 308), then the run aborted at index 308 -- the FIRST epic, epic-1 -- with 'The file (markdown) backend is read-only.' So 0 of 106 epics and 0 of 41 dependency edges migrated. Epic MEMBERSHIP does survive: 242 of the 308 map entries carry epicId metadata, consistent with backend-adapters.spec.md:49 which says epicId/planRef filters read from .beads-map.json because beads does not track them natively. What is missing is the epic ENTITIES (title, status, milestone) and every dependency edge. SECOND DEFECT observed in the same run: the migrate verb reported created:{issues:0,epics:0} even though 308 issues were demonstrably created -- the counter is not incremented before the abort, so a partially-successful run reports as a total no-op and understates what actually landed. That is dangerous on its own: a re-run looks safe when it is not. (It is in fact idempotent via .beads-map.json, but the report gives no way to know that.) NOTE ON API GENERATION: createEpic emits 'createEpic is deprecated; use create() instead. See task-management charter rev 3' under ADEV_DEPRECATION_WARN=1, so the migrate verb drives a deprecated path. Any fix should decide how epics are represented under beads at all -- most plausibly as tiered issues via the unified create() rather than as a separate entity class -- which is a design decision, not a patch. CURRENT STATE, nothing is live: manifest still reads tasks.backend: json, the json board remains authoritative and complete at 308 issues / 106 epics, and the populated .beads store plus .beads-map.json are present but unwired. Pre-migration snapshot committed at c3d4a875 on branch chore/board-migrate-to-beads.; Closed: ALREADY FIXED ON MAIN. Commit 9dc95701 identified the same root cause ("Epics were delegated to FileAdapter, which is read-only-deprecated, so createEpic threw BACKEND_READ_ONLY_DEPRECATED"), and dcb4f591 ("make beads the single source of truth — delete the sidecar") went further than this issue proposed: it removed .beads-map.json entirely, storing adev ids in br external_ref, metadata in br agent_context, and epics as br issues with issue_type: epic. That is the same charter-derived conclusion this issue reached (an epic is a root-level WorkItem, not a separate entity) but implemented without a second store that can disagree. A local fix was written independently (commit 34a5c685, 8 TDD tests) and is DISCARDED as redundant; reflog only. Verified fixed: migration against main creates 106 epic-* external_refs with 0 errors. Also note the created-counter misreporting flagged here is still live on main -- a run that demonstrably created 106 epics reported created:{epics:0}, skipped:106. Rolled into issue-628.
issues.next_action: Decide how epics are represented on the beads backend (likely tiered issues via unified create(), not a separate entity), then fix createEpic and the created-counter reporting. Blocks any complete json->beads migration.

issues.title: json -> beads migration RENUMBERS every issue and loses the source-id mapping, breaking dependencies and all cross-references
issues.notes: Found 2026-08-13 on the first migration run that got far enough to expose it -- only reachable after fixing issue-626 (--db path) and issue-627 (epic creation). BLOCKS any json->beads migration; do not flip tasks.backend until this is fixed. WHAT HAPPENS: BeadsAdapter.create() assigns a fresh sequential id -- nextId = 'issue-' + (count of issue- keys in .beads-map.json + 1) -- and keys the map by that NEW id. The source id is never recorded anywhere. The source board's ids are sparse (issue-1..issue-627 with gaps from deletions); the target map is contiguous (issue-1..issue-309). Every issue therefore silently changes identity. VERIFIED CONCRETELY: source issue-625 ('gate doctor verifies a different gate set...') sits at index 306 of the source list and lands as target issue-307. Map entry fields are only {beadsId, next_action, epicId, ...} -- no source_id/original_id. CONSEQUENCE 1, dependencies: the verb passes SOURCE ids to BeadsAdapter.addDependency, which resolves them against .beads-map.json keys that are now TARGET ids, so lookups miss. Observed dependencies_replayed: 5 of 41, with 'No beads mapping for issue: issue-615 / issue-557 / issue-622' warnings. The 5 that survived are coincidental matches where a source id happened to equal its own index. 36 of 41 edges silently dropped, including the epic-108 wave sequencing (554->552, 555->552, 615->555, 614->559, 557->585/586, 623->557, 625->552/554). CONSEQUENCE 2, far worse and NOT reported at all: every human-readable cross-reference breaks. Issue notes across this board reference other issues by id ('tracked as issue-623', 'see issue-557', 'this is issue-584 in the wild'), as do commit messages, PR descriptions, and spec files. After migration those ids resolve to DIFFERENT issues. Nothing warns; the board looks complete and internally consistent while silently meaning something else. ASYMMETRY WORTH NOTING: the reverse direction already solves this -- runLiveMigration stamps 'original_id: <sourceId>' into notes for beads->json specifically so a re-run can dedupe. json->beads has no equivalent. FIX DIRECTIONS: preserve the source id as the map key (target ids are an implementation detail of beads and need not be resequenced), or at minimum record source_id in each map entry and resolve addDependency through it; and have the verb FAIL LOUDLY rather than warn-and-continue when an edge cannot be resolved, since a silently partial dependency graph is indistinguishable from a complete one. Also fix the created-counter reporting noted in issue-627 (a run that created 308 issues reported created:{issues:0}). STATE: fully rolled back. .beads, .beads-map.json and .migrate-state.json removed; manifest still tasks.backend: json; json board authoritative and complete at 309 issues / 106 epics. Pre-migration snapshot committed at c3d4a875 on branch chore/board-migrate-to-beads. PROCESS NOTE for whoever retries: .migrate-state.json persists a resume cursor (lastSuccessfulIndex). Wiping .beads and .beads-map.json WITHOUT deleting it causes the next run to resume mid-stream and silently migrate almost nothing -- observed as created:{issues:1} against a 309-issue board. Arguably the verb should detect an empty target map against a non-zero resume cursor and refuse.
issues.next_action: Preserve source ids across json->beads (map key or source_id field), resolve addDependency through them, and fail loudly on unresolvable edges. Then retry: rm -rf .beads .context-index/tasks/.beads-map.json .context-index/tasks/.migrate-state.json && br init && adev issues migrate --to beads --include-closed.

issues.title: Migration drops closed status on ISSUES (epics only get the post-create status update)
issues.notes: Found 2026-08-13 flipping tasks.backend to beads after issue-628's id-preservation fix. BLOCKS the flip; reverted to json. beads-adapter.mjs carries the correct comment at line ~522 -- 'br create has no status flag; closed states must go through' a follow-up update -- but implements it ONLY inside createEpic (line ~525, guarded on epic.status === closed). create() has no equivalent, so every closed ISSUE lands open. MEASURED on this repo's 310-issue / 106-epic board: source is 183 closed + 123 open + 4 deferred issues and 79 closed + 27 open epics, so 262 items should be closed. beads held exactly 79 closed -- precisely the epic count -- and 337 open. All 183 closed issues arrived as open, and the 4 deferred ones are unaccounted for (br's status vocabulary may not include deferred; unverified). WHY P0 rather than cosmetic: the flipped board is not merely incomplete, it is actively misleading. '/adev:issues ready' and every 'what should I work on' path would surface 183 completed issues as actionable, and closing them again would be indistinguishable from real work. A board that under-reports is recoverable; one that misrepresents finished work as open corrupts planning. FIX: mirror createEpic's post-create status update inside create(), and decide the mapping for 'deferred' (br may need it expressed differently, or the migration must fail loudly rather than silently coerce). SCOPE OBSERVATION worth attention beyond this issue: this is the FIFTH distinct fidelity defect found in the json->beads path today, each hidden behind the last -- issue-626 (--db pointed at the directory), issue-627 (epics delegated to a read-only adapter), issue-628 (source ids discarded, 0 of 41 dependency edges replayed), then dependencies not reading back through get() after a successful replay (unfiled, needs its own investigation), and now status. Per the debug skill's own rule that repeated failures indicate an architectural problem rather than a series of bugs, the recommendation is a round-trip FIDELITY TEST -- migrate a fixture board, read it back through the adapter, and assert field-by-field equality on ids, status, dependencies, epic membership, milestone and notes -- before this path is trusted with a real board. Every defect so far was found by hand on a live migration, which is not a durable way to gain confidence. CURRENT STATE: tasks.backend reverted to json and verified reading correctly (123 open, matching source). The populated .beads store is left in place, unwired, and is safe to delete.
issues.next_action: Mirror createEpic post-create status update inside create(); decide the deferred mapping; then build a round-trip fidelity test before retrying the flip.

issues.title: BeadsAdapter never reads dependencies back — _toIssue() omits the field entirely
issues.notes: Found 2026-08-13 by a round-trip fidelity check after migrating this repo's 311-issue board. IMPORTANT: this is a READ gap, not data loss. The edges are correctly stored in beads -- 'br list -s all --json' shows 31 items with dependency_count > 0, and issue-628 correctly reports 2 (its edges to issue-626 and issue-627), matching what the migration reported (dependencies_replayed: 44). But every issue returned by BeadsAdapter.list() and .get() comes back with dependencies undefined/empty, because _toIssue() maps title/status/priority/type and the agent_context fields and never populates dependencies. MEASURED: source board has 44 dependency edges; 44 of 44 are absent on read-back through the adapter. CONSEQUENCE: anything that reasons about blocking relationships is silently wrong on the beads backend. '/adev:issues ready' is specified as 'open AND unblocked' and filters on dependencies -- with none visible, every blocked issue reports as ready. The wave sequencing recorded on epic-108 (554->552, 555->552, 615->555, 614->559, 557->585/586, 623->557, 625->552/554) would vanish from every query while remaining perfectly intact in the database. That is the dangerous shape: the data is right, the view is wrong, and nothing errors. FIX: populate dependencies in _toIssue(). br exposes dependency_count/dependent_count on the list record but not the edge endpoints, so the adapter likely needs a 'br dep' query (br dep supports add/import/remove; check for a list/show form) or to resolve edges from a separate pass, mapping br ids back to adev ids via external_ref. Cost note: a naive per-issue dep query is N round trips on a 300+ item board -- prefer a single bulk read if br offers one. VERIFIED CLEAN in the same fidelity run, for scope: ids (310/310 preserved), titles, priority, type, epicId, planRef, spec_ref, next_action, notes -- ZERO mismatches; epics 0 missing with 0 milestone and 0 status mismatches. Only two defects exist on this path now: this one and issue-fw00cl (issue status not migrated).
